title: Signal Sprint: Night Shift Chat

selected_top_5.reasoning: The dominant interaction is typing messages to a fictional guide and receiving contextual, streamed responses inside a messenger-style interface.
The guide functions like a lightweight companion persona who responds to the player and sustains the fantasy of an ongoing relationship/channel.
The experience is more about interface fiction, status signaling, and playful system framing than about a conventional objective-driven challenge loop.
The game presents a runner/courier fantasy and player-directed rerouting, but movement is free target-based drifting rather than true lane-based runner play.
The roleplay-flavored text and staged responses create a small narrative feel, though the structure is far lighter and more toy-like than a real branching story game.

uncertainty_notes: The category universe does not include a perfect fit for an ambient chat toy with tap-to-move background interaction.
Runner-related labels are only partial matches because there are no obstacles, auto-forward progression, or loss conditions.
Narrative labels are also partial matches because the dialogue system is keyword-and-fallback based rather than branching story content.
